The Catholic holy days of obligation in the United States of America are:
January 1: Solemnity of Mary, Mother of God
Ascension of Jesus (celebrated on the Thursday of the sixth week of Easter, or often transferred to the seventh Sunday of Easter)
August 15: Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary
December 8: Immaculate Conception of the Blessed Virgin Mary

December 25: Nativity of the Lord

Other significant Catholic holy days (not days of obligation) include:
January: Epiphany of the Lord
March 19: Saint Joseph, Spouse of the Blessed Virgin Mary
June 24: Nativity of Saint John the Baptist
June 29: Saint Peter and Saint Paul, Apostles
September 8: Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary
September 14: Exaltation of the Holy Cross
October 7: Our Lady of the Rosary
October 28: Saint Simon and Saint Jude, Apostles
December 27: Saint John, Apostle and Evangelist
